name: JellyStations
description: Curate always-on TV stations from your library, surfaced as native Live TV channels.
overview: Curate always-on TV stations from your library.

versions.changelog: A new schedule starts at a program boundary. Until now an edit, a content refresh or Reshuffle now dealt the new schedule from the station's anchor and switched to it at once, usually in the middle of a program, so the stream jumped and the schedule had to patch over the seam. Now the program on the air finishes and its break plays out; the new schedule begins at the next program start on the padding grid (dead air hands over at once). The guide, the Now line and the editor's preview show the finishing program first, marked as the previous schedule. Series still continue from their next episode and what just aired still rests. Lineup and weather channels are unchanged. The handover is kept with the compiled station, so a server restart in between serves the same programs.

Our household, and why this is playing. Settings gains Our household: the Jellyfin users whose play history a station may read. Each station then has two switches on its content step, both off by default. Skip what we finished in the last N days leaves out any film or episode everyone in the household has played within that many days (by Jellyfin's played flag and last-played date); it comes back by itself once the days have passed. Follow our progress starts a series at the first episode nobody has watched and skips ahead as the household watches, in the episodes-in-order play orders, and never goes back behind where the channel already is. Something counts as watched when everyone ticked has played it. Both are read when the station is compiled, so the schedule stays the same for every viewer; every half hour the plugin looks at the household's history and recompiles the stations where it has moved, and the guide follows. The schedule preview, the Now line and the content view now say why each program is there: the block or pool and its play order, the source that brought it in, its place in a marathon, the family-hours rule in force and whether the household's progress placed it. The When step gets Shape the day like a channel: Kids by day, Family evenings, Grown-up nights or Weekend movie marathons write the family hours in one go and, on a shuffled station, add a prime-time block filled with the pool's sources. Fix: saving the Settings page deleted every saved week layout (1.33.0.0). API: HouseholdUserIds in Settings, GET Household/Users, Household on a station, Why on schedule entries, Source on playable items.

Week layouts, and block templates that travel. A week layout is a whole broadcast week of time blocks in one piece. Three ship with the plugin: Classic broadcast week (cartoons on weekday mornings and all Saturday morning, reruns through the day, a Sunday matinee, a movie every night at eight, grown-up shows late, nothing above PG-13 before eight), Movies all day (a family matinee, the main feature at eight, a late movie, shuffled films between) and Kids by day, grown-ups by night. Suggest stations now offers them first, under Broadcast week: each block is filled from the library by what it is for (everything rated G or below for cartoons, half-hour comedies for reruns or every show when there are too few, movies rated PG or below for the matinee, PG-13 and up for late night), with everything else in the pool between the blocks, and a block the library has nothing for is left out and named. The same preview, draft and create buttons apply. In the editor, the dropdown next to Add block lists the layouts: one adds all its blocks at once, without sources, for you to fill. Save blocks as layout keeps a station's blocks (and its family hours) as a layout of your own, with or without their sources; a layout saved with its sources is offered under Suggest stations too, and one saved under a built-in's name takes its place. Saved layouts are listed in Settings and travel with Export and Import. Block templates: the bookmark on a block now asks for a name and whether to keep the sources, so a template can carry its shows or only its shape. When a saved template or a layout is added to a station, any source whose id this server does not know (a template imported from another server, a library removed and added again) is matched by title the way Import does, and what cannot be matched is dropped and said. API: GET/POST/DELETE /JellyStations/WeekLayouts, POST WeekLayouts/{id}/Apply, POST BlockTemplates/{id}/Apply; the export document is version 3 and carries WeekLayouts. Three more things in the same release. A time block can carry a guide title (Saturday Morning Cartoons, The Late Movie): the Jellyfin guide shows it as the title of every program the block plays, with the program's own title on the episode line; changing it redraws the guide without reshuffling the station. Programs are marked New or Repeat in the guide from the station's air history (new when the item has not aired on that station before), and anything rated G, TV-Y, TV-Y7 or TV-G is marked Kids; the schedule preview shows the same New badge. Save blocks as layout now asks what Suggest stations should fill each block with from the library (its own sources, everything, kids, family, family movies, movies, reruns or grown-up) and what plays between the blocks, so a layout of your own is offered there the way the built-in ones are. API: GuideTitle on a time block and on schedule entries; Fills and Filler on POST WeekLayouts.

Picture check: interlacing the flags do not show. Some files are flagged progressive but carry the lines of interlacing in their picture (a DVD or broadcast source encoded without deinterlacing), so Deinterlacing "When the file is interlaced" passed them by and the lines reached the channel. Every file a station plays that could be one (flagged progressive, SDR, up to 1080 lines, at 25 or 30 frames a second) is now looked at once, in the background: up to three six-second samples through ffmpeg's idet filter at low priority, well under a second a file on the test machine, with the answer kept until the file changes. A file counts when at least a quarter of the sampled frames show fields and nearly all of those agree on one field order; grain and starved encodes show both orders and are left alone. The files found are deinterlaced on air with the field order found, and the program up next on a running channel is looked at first. The Status page gets a Picture check section with the progress and the files found. Stations whose Deinterlacing is Always or Off are not looked at. Every station is recompiled once at startup to record picture height and frame rate; schedules do not move. API: GET /JellyStations/PictureCheck.

Choose the scaler, and an editor fix. The encoding settings gain Scaling: the algorithm that resizes every program to the channel's picture size, up or down. Bicubic stays the default; Lanczos keeps more edge detail, most visible when a smaller source is scaled up, at close to twice the scaling work and with faint halos on very hard edges; Spline is smooth and the costliest; Bilinear is the softest. It is ffmpeg's software scaler in every case, none adds detail the file does not have, and the cost is small next to the encode. A station can set its own with the rest of its encoding, and weather screens scaled up on a channel above 1080 lines use it too. Fix: opening a station in the editor could lose settings. When one of its source lists held a single movie or episode next to a wider source (a series, genre, library or folder), the editor asked the server what was already covered while it was still filling in the form, and that request read the half-filled form back into the station: its own encoding was shown as off and a save removed it, and with such a list in the bumpers the mode, time zone and other fields could be replaced the same way. The form is now read only once it is filled. A station that lost its own encoding this way needs it set again. API: Scaler on an encoding profile (bicubic, lanczos, spline, bilinear).

4K channels and starter blocks. The Resolution list in the encoding settings offers 3840 x 2160 (4K). A channel has one picture size, so a 4K movie on a 1080p station is scaled down and a station set to 4K airs everything at 4K. With libx264 the H.264 level is now raised by itself when the size and frame rate need more than the one set (5.1 for 4K, 4.2 for 1080p at 60 fps); before, the stream carried the level as typed. Encoding check: a profile that is likely to disappoint is flagged at the top of the encoding form as you type, as an Encoding badge on the row of a station with its own profile, and on the Status page, where a weak default encoding is listed once however many stations follow it. It flags 4K from an H.264 encoder, a video bitrate too low for the picture (under 10000 kbps at 4K, 6000 at 1440p, 3000 at 1080p, 1500 at 720p, 600 below; HEVC about two thirds of that; half as much again at 50 or 60 fps), one so high it only costs bandwidth (two and a half times the figure that suits the size, such as 20000 kbps left on a station that went back to 1080p), and audio under 96 kbps; each names the figure that suits. Picking a size in the Resolution list now also moves the video bitrate to the figure that suits it (3500 at 720p, 8000 at 1080p, 20000 at 4K, less with an HEVC encoder below 4K) while the field still holds the suggested figure for the size you are leaving; a bitrate you set yourself is not touched. Every expanding source (library, genre, tag, series, collection, playlist) can be limited by picture size: 4K only, 1080p or better, 720p or better, by the size Jellyfin read from each file, so a 4K channel can play only 4K files and scale nothing up. Starter blocks: the dropdown next to "Add block" now offers Saturday morning cartoons, Prime-time movie, Late night and Weather on the hour beside your saved templates; they come with days, time and play order and without sources, and a template saved under the same name replaces one. Two fixes found while testing 4K: the stream kept only the last 2 MB for a viewer joining, less than one keyframe interval above about 8000 kbps, so a tune-in on a high-bitrate channel could start between keyframes and show nothing or garbage for up to the interval; it now keeps two intervals at the channel's bitrate. Weather screens are drawn at 1080 lines at most and scaled up on a larger channel, a tune-in no longer waits for a whole segment of screens to be drawn (the first segment is cut at what about 6 seconds of drawing gives and the rest are drawn while it plays), so a weather channel with several places and radar opens in seconds after a new hour or new reports. API: MinResolution on a content source, GET BlockTemplates/BuiltIn, EncodingWarnings per station and DefaultEncodingWarnings on GET Health.

Problem files on the Status page. A file that gives trouble on a channel is now remembered after the stream stops and across restarts, with its path, what went wrong, ffmpeg's own line and the station: a file that was missing or could not be opened, one ffmpeg could not play, one that stopped before its listed end (cut off, or shorter than Jellyfin has it), one that played with decode errors, one the GPU decoder failed on, and a clip folder file ffprobe could not read. A file leaves the list when it next plays through cleanly from its start, when it has been replaced or removed (looked at when the page opens and on Refresh now), or when you dismiss it. API: GET and DELETE ProblemFiles, DELETE ProblemFiles/{id}.

Bumper clips from a folder. The bumper, pre-roll and post-roll sources in the station editor take a folder on the server as well as library items: type its path under the search box and press "Add folder". Every video file in it and its subfolders becomes a clip, so idents and bumps no longer need a Jellyfin library (a Movies or Shows library drops files it cannot match to a title). A name without a path is a folder under data/JellyStations/bumpers in the Jellyfin data folder. Each file is read once with ffprobe and remembered until it changes; a file that cannot be read is listed with the station's excluded items. New files are picked up when the station's content is refreshed (nightly, or Refresh content). API: Path on a Folder content source, GET Library/ClipFolder.

Preview a day on the suggestions page. The clock button on a suggested station opens the next 24 hours it would play, with the time zone and the look and breaks chosen at the top of the page, before anything is created. Changing the time zone or the look rebuilds the open previews. A shuffled channel draws its order again when it is created, so the preview is a sample day and not the exact first one. More suggestion rules: a genre with enough hours in movies and again in episodes becomes two channels ("Comedy Movies", "Comedy TV"); Anime and Documentaries channels from every genre and tag that spell the same thing; "Comfort Reruns" of the half-hour comedies together; decade channels for shows ("1990s TV"). Suggestions know what is on the air: each shows the hours no enabled channel plays yet, the list leads with the most new hours, a suggestion whose content is all on a channel already is hidden behind "Show them", and "Everything Else" offers one station of every movie and show no channel plays. "Almost there" under the list names what came close ("Horror: 6.5 h, needs 8"). Settings gains "Station suggestions" with the amount each kind of channel needs; it replaces the "Include small channels" box on the suggestions page. A library of nothing but short clips (a Home Videos library of bumps or idents) is now read, kept out of the library figures, never made a channel, and offered as "Bumper clips from" so the stations you create play those clips in their breaks. API: POST Suggestions/Preview, GET Suggestions/Report, BumperLibraryId on Create, Draft and Preview.

Fixes a server crash loop. On a pool station that plays episodes in order, anything that started a new revision (saving a changed station, a recompile that found new content, Reshuffle) continued each series from its next episode but kept the slot times of the order before that move. Episodes of different lengths then left an instant no program covered, the schedule repeated one empty entry without end, and reading it (the guide refresh, the air log's minute tick) used up the server's memory until Jellyfin was killed and restarted, over and over (1.25.0.0 to 1.26.1.0). The slot times now follow the order that airs, and a schedule that does not move forward stops instead of repeating. Affected stations get a correct timeline on the first start with this version; nothing needs to be edited.

Square pixels on every program. A source with non-square pixels (DVD rips, 720x480 or 720x576 shown as 4:3 or 16:9) was fitted by its stored size and its pixel shape was passed into the channel's stream, so the picture came out the wrong width, the shape changed from program to program, and Jellyfin's cached probe could announce the whole channel as anamorphic; some players (seen with Moonfin on tvOS) then showed the picture squeezed. The picture is now fitted by its display aspect ratio and every program leaves as the same square-pixel frame. Each station gets a new stream id once, so Jellyfin probes it afresh instead of serving the old anamorphic description (the first tune-in after the update takes about 3 seconds longer). When the encoder produces no data within 20 seconds of a tune-in, the server log now carries a warning that names the file and ffmpeg's last lines.

Plugin-wide defaults for the logo bug and the "Up next" card. Settings gains a "Logo bug and Up next card" section with the same controls a station has; every station follows them unless it sets its own on the Logo step of its editor ("Set the logo bug for this station", "Set the Up next card for this station"), where the hint says what the default currently is and the form starts from it. Saving a changed default restarts only the streams of the stations that follow it. "Use on every station" next to each default drops the stations' own settings so all of them follow it again (POST /JellyStations/Settings/ClearOverrides/{LogoOverlay|UpNextCard}). Existing stations are brought over once at startup: a bug or card that was off now follows the default (which starts off, so nothing changes on the air), one that was on stays the station's own; imported stations and saved templates from older versions are treated the same. In the JSON a station without its own carries no logoOverlay / upNextCard, and GET /JellyStations/Settings returns both defaults; the station list says which stations set their own (OwnLogoOverlay, OwnUpNextCard).

Air history. The plugin now keeps an air log per station: once a minute it notes which programs each enabled station aired (a slot that aired counts, viewer or not; a gap longer than an hour while the server was off is not back-filled). When an edit, a content change or the new Reshuffle action starts a new revision, the log is frozen into the compile and the new schedule continues from it: with episodes in order, every series carries on from the episode after the one that aired last (by number when that episode is gone) instead of going back to episode 1; a Sequential or episodes-in-order time block resumes after the item it aired last and the between-block stream skips what it had already played this pass; the series or film that was airing when the revision changed never leads the new schedule, and the cooldown rests what the previous revision just aired. A recompile of unchanged content keeps the timeline byte for byte, and a station with no history schedules exactly as before. The station row gains History (what aired, when and how often, with a Clear button) and Reshuffle now (a fresh order from this moment that still continues every series); schedule rows, the content table and the Now line say when a title last aired and how often. New endpoints: GET and DELETE /JellyStations/Stations/{id}/History, POST /JellyStations/Stations/{id}/Reshuffle; schedule and content entries carry LastAiredUtc and AirCount. The log lives in the data folder under history/ and is not part of an export.

Suggested stations arrive finished. Each station created from Suggest stations now gets a drawn logo (the editor's generated card, drawn on the server with the same seeded patterns and colors), the time zone and the first channel number chosen on the page (numbers already in use are skipped), and, with a station template picked under "Look and breaks from", that template's bumpers, pre-roll and post-roll, weather in the breaks, logo overlay, up next card, encoding, padding, card text and family hours, while the content stays the suggester's. A pencil on every suggestion opens it in the editor as an unsaved station with those options applied and the logo ready to upload on save, so it can be changed before it is created (POST /JellyStations/Suggestions/Draft). The Create result lists a warning for any station whose logo could not be drawn. Deinterlacing: interlaced files (DVD rips, broadcast captures) are now deinterlaced by the plugin before scaling, so the combing no longer ends up in the stream. The encoding profile gets a Deinterlacing setting: When the file is interlaced (the default, following the field order Jellyfin probed), Always (for files whose flags are missing) or Off; on a 50 or 60 fps profile every field becomes a frame so video-shot material keeps its motion. Stations are recompiled once at startup to record which files are interlaced, and the hardware test deinterlaces the same way.

Smarter franchise detection and a Classic Movies suggestion. Suggest stations now groups movies by the collection their metadata provider puts them in (TMDB's "James Bond Collection" and the like, stamped on every member whether or not Jellyfin builds the box set), so a series whose titles share nothing (Dr. No, Goldfinger, Skyfall) gets its marathon and its Franchise Nights slot; two members are enough, and the "Collection" suffix is dropped from the name. Titles without a collection are still grouped by shared prefix as before. A new "Classic Movies" suggestion offers every movie made before 1970 as one shuffled station once they total 8 hours, since old films rarely reach the decade rule's 8 hours one decade at a time; the cut-off year and the hours are thresholds, and the small-library toggle lowers the hours like the other rules. The station it creates is the same as setting a Movies library source to movies only with To year 1969, which any source could already do.

Weather on ordinary stations shares the weather channel. A station with a weather time block or local weather in the breaks no longer keeps places of its own: its Weather section is a dropdown naming the weather channel whose places, look and music it shows (the first weather channel when none is picked), so forecasts, alerts and radar are fetched once per place however many stations air them, and the music plays in step with the channel. The stations own logo is still drawn on the screens. A weather channels editor lists the stations that air its places. Stations that had their own places from 1.20 or 1.21 switch to the weather channel on the next save; without one the editor says so and the block and breaks show a card until it exists. Hardening from a security review: a stations logo file name is no longer taken from a create request or an import (the anonymous logo endpoint could otherwise be pointed at any file the server can read), logo paths are checked to stay in the logos folder, uploaded logos must be real PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF files and are refused past 5 MB before being read, extra ffmpeg arguments and the hardware device in an imported encoding profile are cleared and listed in the import result, the schedule window is capped at 21 days however it is asked for, the RainViewer tile host must be an https rainviewer.com address, weather and radar requests no longer follow redirects or read unbounded bodies, and music pack downloads stop at the published length. Fixes: "New channel with selected" on the Not on a channel page opened an empty draft; block templates lost their kind and repeat settings; the editors cycle length left out the bumper break; the weather screen folders of all but one station were never swept; a garbled tick mark on the Health page. Stations are now listed in channel-number order everywhere (Health, Export and the hardware test sorted 10 before 2). A large internal consolidation of duplicated code with no other intended change in behaviour.

Station templates. "Save as template" on a station editors first step keeps everything but the content (mode, order, padding, family hours, cooldown, time blocks with their days and times but no shows, bumpers and their clips, the weather look without places or music, logo color, logo bug, up-next card, encoding, seasonal windows, excluded tags, minimum runtime, card text) under a name of your choice. Saved templates appear first on the New station page; the nine presets are now templates served by the plugin (GET /JellyStations/StationTemplates) rather than a list in the page, and a template saved under a presets name takes its place until it is deleted (Settings lists the saved ones). Duplicate on a station row opens a copy with the content and logo included under the next channel number. Export now writes one document with the stations and the saved station and block templates; Import takes that document or the old bare array of stations and replaces templates by name. Saving Settings can no longer drop templates.

Alerts and title cards on the weather channel. While a place has a watch, warning or advisory in force, the channel shows an alerts screen for it before its current conditions: each alert with its severity colour, when it runs (in the place's own time), the area it covers and as much of its text as fits, up to three alerts per screen with the rest counted; the current, hourly and 7-day screens carry a one-line strip meanwhile. Alerts come from the US National Weather Service's free API (no key; United States and territories only, places elsewhere skip the screen), are checked every five minutes while the station is on and cached under data/JellyStations/weather/alerts. Each place now opens with a short title card (its name and region over a faint icon of its conditions, 3 seconds by default, 1 to 10) so the eye knows the channel has moved on. Both are on by default, with checkboxes in the editor; the forecast status gets an Alerts column and Preview screen can show both screens. Weather on ordinary stations: a time block can now play the local weather instead of programs (What plays: Local weather), and any block can repeat every N minutes until a time, so "the weather at the top of every hour" is a 5-minute weather block at 06:00 repeating every 60 minutes; the bumpers section gains Local weather in the breaks, a short run of the weather screens (up to a set length, before or after the clips) in every break with at least 45 seconds of room. Both use the station's Weather section, which appears in the editor when needed. Music levelling: every weather music track is measured once in the background (ffmpeg loudnorm) and played at -18 LUFS with peaks under -1 dB, on by default, with a status line in the editor; tracks fade out and in at their boundaries.

Forecast radar on the weather channel. After the local radar each place now gets a forecast radar screen on the same map: where NOAA's HRRR model (a new run every hour, 15-minute steps out to 18 hours) expects the rain and snow to go, from now out to a configurable look-ahead (1 to 18 hours, default 3) at a configurable step (15 or 30 minutes or an hour, default 15); the loop is kept to 25 frames, so a long look-ahead at a short step plays at the next step up. The header names the time each frame is a forecast for and the map credits the model run. Tiles come from the Iowa Environmental Mesonet, so the screen is for places in the contiguous United States only; other places skip it. The plugin finds the newest published run by probing, fetches the frames from now to the look-ahead plus two hours, tops the window up as the clock moves, and caches them under data/JellyStations/weather/radar/<place>/forecast. The editor gets the checkbox, the look-ahead and step selects, a Forecast radar column in the forecast status, Fetch now and Preview screen for it. Existing weather stations get the screen; untick Show the forecast radar screen to go back.

Local radar on the weather channel. After each place's current conditions the channel now shows a loop of the last three quarters of an hour of precipitation radar over a map of the area, with nearby towns, a light-to-heavy legend and the frame clock. NOAA NEXRAD (through the Iowa Environmental Mesonet's time-enabled WMS) covers places in the contiguous United States; RainViewer covers the rest of the world. Frames are fetched every five minutes while the station is on, only the new ones each time, and cached under data/JellyStations/weather/radar. The map (coasts, lakes, borders, towns) is Natural Earth data packed into the plugin and drawn in the theme's colours, with four map areas to choose from (metro, state, regional, wide). The editor's forecast status shows the radar source and frame count per place, Fetch now refreshes radar too, and Preview screen can show the radar screen. Existing weather stations get the radar screen; untick Show the local radar screen to go back.

Audio language and subtitles per source. Every content source (a series, a season, a collection, a genre...) can now name the audio language its items play in and a subtitle language to burn into the picture, with an option to burn them only when that audio language is missing from a file, so an anime station can run one show in Japanese with English subtitles next to dubbed ones. The editor reads the languages actually present on the source files (GET /JellyStations/Library/Items/{id}/Languages) and lists them with file counts. Text tracks (SRT, ASS, MP4 text, WebVTT, external files) are rendered by libass after scaling and tone mapping; PGS and DVD bitmap tracks are overlaid on the source picture; embedded text tracks are extracted once into data/JellyStations/subtitles so program starts do not read the whole file, and the next program track is extracted while the current one plays. Language codes match across spellings (ja, jpn; ger, deu). Press Refresh content after changing a source tracks. Also in this release, from 1.16.2.0: browser playback fixed (Jellyfin flags every plugin channel interlaced unless it probes the stream; probing is back on with a media source id derived from the station and its output format, the container is declared as ts so the aac_adtstoasc filter is applied, and a reader joining a channel starts at a keyframe).

The encoding profile's preset now reaches the hardware encoders: Quick Sync (h264_qsv, hevc_qsv) gets it in its own vocabulary (veryfast to veryslow; ultrafast and superfast become veryfast) and NVENC gets p1 to p7 (x264 words translated, veryfast is p2); VA-API, AMF and VideoToolbox, which have no preset option, get none, and a blank preset leaves the encoder default. Until now only libx264 and libx265 saw the preset, so hevc_qsv ran at its default medium: on an i5-8500T an HDR10 channel went from 2.0x to 3.5x real time with the default veryfast. README notes CPU passthrough for VMs (zscale needs AVX2).

HDR channels. A profile's new Output setting (SDR, the default, or HDR10) makes a station a 10-bit BT.2020 PQ HEVC Main 10 channel: HDR10 programs keep their range and mastering metadata, HLG is converted to PQ, and SDR programs, slates, cards, the logo and weather screens are converted into the PQ container at SDR brightness, so the stream never changes format. Needs an HEVC encoder (libx265, hevc_qsv, hevc_nvenc, hevc_vaapi, hevc_amf, hevc_videotoolbox); HDR-capable clients direct play it and Jellyfin tone maps it for the rest (turn on tone mapping under Dashboard > Playback > Transcoding). The channel is declared as hevc Main 10 to Jellyfin instead of being probed (Jellyfin caches a channel's first probe for good, and skipping the probe makes tune-in quicker), the Hardware section lists the HEVC encoders in the ffmpeg build, Hardware Test takes an OutputRange override, and the Status page shows HDR10 out. Weather guide programs carry the station logo as their thumbnail (1.15.1.0).

Renamed to JellyStations. The plugin, its DLL (Jellyfin.Plugin.JellyStations.dll), the dashboard page, the API routes (/JellyStations/...) and the data folder (data/JellyStations) carry the new name. The plugin id is unchanged, so Jellyfin treats this as an update of the installed TvStation, an existing data/TvStation folder is moved to data/JellyStations on first start, and Live TV channels keep their ids. Plugin repository: add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jdaubert12/JellyStations/main/manifest.json under Dashboard > Plugins > Repositories to install and update from the catalog. The example stations now carry placeholder titles.

Weather channel: the music line on the screens now reads "Now playing: title – artist" (or just the title when no artist is known) instead of the bare title and artist. The editor checkbox that turns the line off is unchanged.

Chance of rain, snow, mix or ice. Open-Meteo gives one chance of precipitation that covers rain, showers and snow together, so the percentage on the hourly strip, the 7-day forecast and the current conditions panel now says what it is a chance of: "rain", "snow", "mix" (rain and snow both forecast) or "ice" (freezing rain or drizzle). The type comes from the hourly and daily rain, showers and snowfall amounts now fetched with the forecast, else from the weather code, else from the temperature (at or below freezing it would fall as snow). Snow days on the 7-day forecast quote the snowfall depth ("5 in snow", "13 cm snow") instead of the melt-water total. The hourly strip puts the word on its own line under the percentage.

Weather channel: a new station mode that shows current conditions, the next twelve hours and the week ahead for up to eight places, drawn by the plugin as full-screen graphics (three colour themes, the station logo, a live clock in each place's own time zone) that cross-fade and cycle like the cable weather channel, with an optional "on the 8s" pass at :08, :18, :28..., a travel-cities screen and hourly guide entries titled from the places. Forecasts come from Open-Meteo (free, no account; only each place's latitude and longitude is sent), polled every 15 minutes, cached on disk, and the screens say when a forecast is older than the station allows. Music plays underneath from Jellyfin music (playlists, albums, artists, music genres, tracks) and/or every audio file in a folder on the server, in a seeded shuffle that is the same for every viewer and crosses segment boundaries without a gap, with the track title and artist on screen. The editor gets a Weather channel preset, place search, a music picker, a forecast status table with Fetch now, and screen previews. New endpoints under /TvStation/Weather (Search, Status, Refresh, Preview). The plugin ships no music; use tracks you have the right to play. Also: the Inter font (SIL OFL) is embedded for the screens. Music packs: the editor lists curated instrumental sets under licences that allow playing and passing them on; "Get it" fetches each track from the artist's own site into data/TvStation/music/<pack>/ with a SHA-256 check and a CREDITS.txt (starter pack: thirty Kevin MacLeod lounge and light jazz pieces, CC BY 4.0; optional: HoliznaCC0 lo-fi jazz guitar, CC0, downloaded by hand from the Free Music Archive). The music folder setting takes several folders separated by ";".

Fix: a station could keep encoding for nobody. Jellyfin only reports a viewer gone when the client says so or its connection to the server closes, so an app that was killed, a TV switched off on a channel or a dropped network connection left the viewer count stuck at 1 and ffmpeg running with no one reading the stream, sometimes for hours. The plugin now stops any station stream nobody has read for longer than the new "Stop an unwatched stream after" setting (default 120 seconds; 0 turns it off), whatever the viewer count says, and logs that it did. Linger is unchanged. Station editor: the Advanced section (call sign, padding grid, schedule anchor, station card text, encoding) was only shown under "All settings"; it now sits at the bottom of every step.

"Up next" card. A station can draw a translucent panel over the last seconds of every program with the next program's title, its poster or episode thumbnail, the season and episode or the year, and its start and end time in the station's time zone (12 or 24-hour clock); choose the corner, the times before the end it appears (one or more, e.g. an hour, half an hour and five minutes), how long it stays, its height and opacity, whether to show the artwork and the times, and how it arrives and leaves (fade, slide in from the side, both, or neither). It is burned into the stream by the plugin's ffmpeg, so every viewer sees it in step with the picture whatever the client's HLS delay. Bumper clips and station breaks are skipped when choosing what to announce; programs too short for the card do without it; a card ffmpeg cannot draw is dropped for the session with a note on the station row. Off by default. Fix: QSV (Intel Quick Sync) decoding failed on every file with "Impossible to convert between the formats" and "Conversion failed", so stations and the hardware test never got Intel hardware decoding. ffmpeg 7's "-hwaccel qsv" leaves the *_qsv decoders' frames on GPU surfaces the software filters cannot read; the plugin now names the QSV decoder for the file's codec (h264_qsv, hevc_qsv, mpeg2_qsv, vc1_qsv, vp8_qsv, vp9_qsv, av1_qsv) on a QSV device created up front, which decodes to system memory, and a file whose codec was never recorded stays in software. The hardware test now confirms the decoder from ffmpeg's stream mapping (a *_qsv or *_cuvid decoder) or from the GPU device node ffmpeg holds open while it runs (Linux, software encoder); an explicit VA-API, CUDA, D3D11VA or VideoToolbox hwaccel that reports no fallback but cannot be confirmed from outside is "unverified" rather than a problem. Fix: with the h264_qsv, h264_nvenc or h264_amf encoder a client tuning in mid-program got audio but no video until the next program started (Jellyfin's remux of the channel logged "non-existing PPS 0 referenced" and wrote no video for 78 s): those encoders turn a forced key frame into a plain I frame without headers that no demuxer treats as a key frame, so they now set key frames by GOP alone, as Jellyfin does, and every GOP starts with an IDR frame and its SPS/PPS. libx264 and the VA-API encoders keep forced key frames.

Stream health. Status shows, per active session, what the encoder is really doing: the hardware decoder confirmed by the GPU device node ffmpeg holds open (Linux), or flagged when ffmpeg fell back to software or the device failed; the encoder; HDR tone mapping; CPU cores in use; and how far ahead of real time the encoder runs, with a plain-language problem line when a station stutters or stalls. A Hardware section shows Jellyfin's transcoding setting, what the default profile resolves to, the /dev/dri nodes the server can see and this ffmpeg build's hwaccels, H.264 encoders and tone mapping filters, with notes on anything that does not line up. "Test" runs a few seconds of a station's current program through the real decode, filter and encode chain at full speed and reports which decoder ffmpeg attached and the speed relative to real time (GET /TvStation/Hardware, POST /TvStation/Hardware/Test). Fix: the GPU decoder was handed every file, and ffmpeg's qsv/cuda decoders do not fall back to software on their own, so one file the GPU cannot decode (10-bit H.264, DivX/Xvid, a codec unticked in Jellyfin) exited ffmpeg with "Nothing was written into output file" and switched the whole session to software. Stations now record each file's codec, profile, bit depth and pixel format (one recompile at startup) and decide per file: "Follow Jellyfin" honors Jellyfin's "Enable hardware decoding for" checkboxes and 10-bit HEVC/VP9/RExt toggles, a hand-picked decoder takes everything GPUs can decode; the rest plays in software and the Status page says why. If the decoder still refuses a file, only that program is replayed in software; a device-level failure, or a second program failing, still turns the session to software. Faults name the program and quote ffmpeg's first error line rather than its last.

Stream fixes from a stuttering-playback diagnosis. HDR sources (PQ or HLG) are tone mapped to SDR BT.709 and stripped of HDR side data, and every segment is tagged BT.709, so clients no longer re-encode a channel because of "video range type"; stations are recompiled once at startup to record which items are HDR. Hardware decoding: new "Hardware decoding" and "Hardware device" fields on the encoding profile (default "Follow Jellyfin", which mirrors Dashboard > Playback > Transcoding: qsv, vaapi, cuda, videotoolbox or d3d11va), with the frames handed back to the software filters; a device that fails drops to software decoding for the session. VA-API encoders now get their device and frame upload, so h264_vaapi works. Reported media source carries the BT.709 SDR color tags. Frame rate and bitrate hints: 24 fps for film stations, 3500 kbps for 720p and 8000 for 1080p.

Fix: a movie or episode added to a station by hand is never dropped by an excluded tag, even when a genre, library, collection or playlist source earlier in the same section lists it first. The station list no longer flags "1 empty source" for a hand-picked item that an earlier source already put on the station; a source only counts as empty when it adds nothing that is not already playing. Editor: when a movie already plays through a wider source of the same section (genre, tag, series, collection, playlist or library), search results say "Already included via Genre \"Comedy\"" and the chip of a hand-picked movie shows "also via" that source.

Make a logo from the name: new "Pick the color too" option seeds the card color from the name, number and what the channel plays (remembered per browser); "Another look" then changes the color as well as the pattern.

Make a logo from the name: the card now carries a pattern (gradient, stripes, dots, rings, slabs or color bars) seeded from the name, number and what the channel plays, so each channel looks different while the same station always draws the same card. "Another look" draws the next variation.

Editor: the station's excluded tags, the switch for the plugin-wide excluded tags, and the minimum length now sit in a "Leave out" section on step 2 (What plays), with the Excluded items list under them, instead of under Advanced in All settings.
Fix: the filter box on the Not on a channel page made Jellyfin's page setup throw, which left buttons, inputs and checkboxes across the dashboard unstyled. Install this over 1.10.0.0.

Not on a channel: a dashboard page listing the movies and shows no channel plays (GET /TvStation/Library/Coverage). Tick titles to start a new channel with them or add them to an existing channel's pool, filler or list; shows with only some episodes on a channel are marked; paused channels count only when asked; bumper and ident clips count as on their channel.

Paint the week: the time blocks section shows a seven-day grid. Click or drag on it to add a block (drag sideways to cover several days), click a block to edit it; blocks that cross midnight continue in the next column and non-weekly ones are outlined.

Three-step editor: Name and look (with a logo made from the name), What plays, When; All settings keeps the full form. The editor opens on step 1, remembers when you prefer the full form, and jumps to the step a problem is on when a save is refused.

Cooldown: a pool can rest a show or film for N hours before it plays again (0 = off, Movie night preset uses 8). A gentle rule on the timeline: it holds films apart across the seam between two rounds and spaces out weighted repeats, and gives way when nothing rested is available. Stations with time blocks are not covered yet.

Station rows show the time left in the current program and the next two programs, the last streaming error (permission denied, file not found and an unmounted folder told apart; early ffmpeg exits carry their last log line) with a dismiss button, and health badges from the last compile. The Status view gains a Health section (GET /TvStation/Health): sources that matched nothing, stations under a day of unique content, items skipped for a missing runtime, path or file. Fixes a movie playing twice in a row across the seam between two shuffle cycles: the back-to-back rule now covers movies as well as series. Easier for non-technical people: an empty dashboard opens on what the library could support, New station starts from a preset (Kids channel, Movie night, Holiday channel and more), modes have plain names, Recompile is now Refresh content, daytime rules are Family hours, rarely used settings sit under Advanced, and health warnings carry fix buttons.

Block recurrence: a block can repeat every week (as before), every N weeks from a chosen date, in certain weeks of the month (1st-4th or last; weeks run Monday-Sunday so a weekend stays together), or only on listed dates. Sequential blocks continue across occurrences, so a marathon over two weekends picks up where it left off.

Dashboard: new "Recompile all" button re-scans the library for every station at once (for batches of newly added films) and refreshes the guide once if anything changed. Also available as POST /TvStation/Stations/RecompileAll.

Bumpers: pre-roll idents and post-roll clips. A pre-roll ends every break right before the next program (which still starts on the grid); a post-roll opens the break after one. Each picks from its own sources or the main bumper sources, and is skipped when no clip fits.

Blocks: new per-block option to let the pool or filler finish its last program past the block end instead of cutting it (on for new blocks). Settings page gets a header and sectioned cards; the plugin page now has a title in the dashboard.

Films split across files (Blu-ray part1/part2 that Jellyfin stacks into one movie) are scheduled at their full combined length and play straight through as one program. Also fixes repeated encoder restarts when a file ends a second before its listed runtime.
Fix "Suggest stations" failing to load (GET request sent a body).

Time blocks on Pool stations (a movie block at 18:00 while the pool keeps its shuffle, marathons and daytime rules); logo overlay over the video; Import matches movies, series, seasons, episodes and collections by name on another server; library analysis endpoint; Suggest stations on the dashboard (genres, series, kids and family, franchises, collections, decades, seasonal); block templates; per-station minimum runtime.
